title: Slot-aware phased switchover with traffic-shaping and automated rollback policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The Private runtime rollout path currently relies on coarse canary and node-drain strategies which cause cold KV-cache behavior and bursty tail-latency for tenant workloads during upgrades. We've seen incidents where tenant-specific state and prefix distributions cause long warmup times, resulting in SLA blips during upgrades.

Goal:
Design and implement a slot-aware phased switchover that: (1) minimizes user-visible latency/regressions during data-plane upgrades in VPC/private deployments, (2) pre-warms KV caches intelligently per-tenant slot, (3) shapes traffic across new and old slots to avoid overload, and (4) provides deterministic automated rollback when defined SLO thresholds are breached.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the existing Dedicated autoscaler or global routing layer (we will integrate with them).
- Full rewrite of operator; this is an incremental rollout automation feature scoped to runtime data plane upgrades.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Slot-aware model: treat each runtime worker's execution context as N slots (logical serving paths). For rolling upgrade, create target slot cohorts (small groups ~5-10% of total slots) rather than whole-node swaps. This reduces KV cache invalidation blast radius.

2) Pre-warm/priming phase: before shifting traffic, run a priming job that replays an anonymized representative prefix set (from daily sampling) against the new slot cohort to populate KV/state. Priming uses a read-only snapshot and keeps a priming_success metric per-slot. For tenants with persistent caches we also support loading saved KV snapshots.

3) Traffic shaping: introduce a multi-step traffic curve per cohort: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Each step is gated by health checks/metrics: p95 latency, error rate, kv_hit_rate, caller-level timeouts. Inter-step wait defaults: 2m, 4m, 6m, but adjustable per-tenant. Traffic is routed by the control plane router which supports percentage routing to slot cohorts.

4) Health checks and rollback triggers: use composite gating derived from metrics:
   - runtime.request_latency_p95 (compare baseline)
   - runtime.error_rate (5xx, stream errors)
   - runtime.kv_hit_rate (goal >= 80% for primed prefixes)
   - quality_signals (sandbox evals for synthesis regressions)
Rollback triggers (examples): sustained p95 >= baseline * 1.3 for 3m, absolute error rate increase >= 1% for 2m, or kv_hit_rate < 50% for 5m. When a trigger fires, automated rollback will shift traffic back to previous slot cohort in an exponential backoff pattern and mark the cohort as failed for investigation.

5) Observability and runbook automation: add a rollout dashboard showing cohort-level metrics, auto-open incident runbook on rollback with pre-filled diagnostics (PRs, commit hash, priming logs, sample traces).

6) Safety nets: a global circuit-breaker that prevents more than one cohort in the same shard/tenant from being upgraded concurrently; also tenant-priority weighting to avoid impacting high-SLA accounts.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Phase A: router percentage routing hooks + cohort API (control-plane change) + metric gating engine (2 sprints).
- Phase B: priming job that replays sampled prefixes and slot priming success metrics (1 sprint).
- Phase C: rollout orchestrator that executes phased traffic curves, watches gates, and triggers rollback (1 sprint).
- Phase D: integration tests, canary runs on staging, and documentation + runbooks (1 sprint).

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for gating and rollback logic.
- Integration tests using a synthetic user generator that simulates per-tenant prefix distributions and measures p95 and KV hit behavior under upgrade traffic curves.
- Staging run: deploy to private staging VPC with 3 representative tenants; run multiple upgrades with intentional priming failures to validate rollback.

Metrics to monitor for success:
- Reduction in p95 tail spikes during upgrades vs baseline (% reduction).
- Fewer customer SEV incidents triggered during planned upgrades.
- KV hit rate post-priming >= 80% for primed prefixes.
- Automated rollback correctness (no false positives in >95% of runs).

Migration and operator UX:
- Provide a flag in the operator CRD to opt-in to slot-aware rollout per-runtime. Default will be disabled for older customers and enabled by default for new Private stacks.
- Console will expose rollout progress and allow manual override (pause/resume/abort).

Security and compliance notes:
- Priming replay uses anonymized, sampled prefixes and runs in read-only mode. No user PII should be included; encryption and KMS access patterns unchanged.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Complexity: more stateful orchestration is required; mitigated by incremental rollout phases and feature-flag gating.
- Slightly longer overall upgrade time vs brute-force whole-node swap, but much lower outage risk.

Open questions:
- How to best select representative prefixes for per-tenant priming? (sampling window and retention policy)
- Default thresholds for p95 and error rate: should be tenant-configurable?
- Operator resource requirements for priming (CPU/GPU)?

Next steps:
- Engineering design review with infra and console teams (scheduled 2026-02-18).
- Prototype priming job in staging with synthetic load (owner: Diego).
- Create PR for control-plane cohort API (owner: Felicia Wu).
acceptance_criteria: Slot cohort API implemented and documented in control plane
Priming job can successfully populate KV cache for sampled prefixes and expose priming_success metric
Rollout orchestrator executes traffic curve steps and respects gating metrics
Automated rollback triggers fire for injected failure scenarios in staging
Rollout dashboard shows cohort-level metrics and links to runbook with diagnostics
